drug_class: CDK4/6 inhibitor (a type of targeted cancer therapy)
purpose: Abemaciclib is used to treat certain types of breast cancer that are hormone receptor-positive (HR+) and HER2-negative. It is often used in adults whose cancer has spread to other parts of the body or to help prevent the cancer from coming back after surgery. It is usually taken along with other medicines like hormone therapy.
how_it_works: Cancer cells grow by dividing and multiplying out of control. Abemaciclib works by blocking specific proteins in cancer cells called CDK4 and CDK6, which act like 'on switches' for cell growth. By blocking these switches, the medicine helps slow down or stop cancer cells from dividing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea is very common and can be severe, so stay well hydrated and let your doctor know right away if it starts. Other common side effects include nausea, tiredness, low white blood cell counts (which raises infection risk), low appetite, vomiting, stomach pain, and hair thinning.
warnings: Diarrhea can become serious quickly — start anti-diarrheal medicine like loperamide at the first sign and call your care team. This drug can lower your blood cell counts, increasing your risk of infections, bleeding, and anemia — watch for fever, chills, or unusual bruising. It can also cause rare but serious lung problems (shortness of breath, cough), and liver problems. Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant should use effective birth control, as this medicine can harm an unborn baby. Avoid grapefruit and certain other medicines that interact with this drug.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 150 mg taken by mouth twice a day (about every 12 hours), with or without food. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Take it at the same times each day, and swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or chew them. If you miss a dose, skip it and take the next one at your regular time — do not double up.
